ai.title: Bring your own AI assistant
ai.body: Connect OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, DeepSeek, Mistral, Together, xAI or Fireworks — or a local Ollama or LM Studio. Tidy up, add detail, summarise, or give your own instruction, on the selection or the whole document. Off by default, with no key and no endpoint of ours; keys are encrypted per operating-system account and never touch settings.json. It shows you what it is about to send before it sends it.

trash.title: Deleted documents you can get back
trash.body: Deletes now go to a list inside MarkCraft instead of straight to the system recycle bin, so you can see what went, restore it in one click, or delete it for good. Keeps the 30 most recent by default — change it, or turn the limit off entirely, under Settings → Files.

palettes.title: Six named palettes
palettes.body: Nord, Solarized, Gruvbox, Rosé Pine, Sepia and a high-contrast option, each with a light and a dark form. A palette replaces the greys only, so your accent colour still applies on top of it.

customColors.title: Set individual colours yourself
customColors.body: Twelve colours — window, panels, text, borders, accent and the status colours — can be overridden one at a time and reset one at a time, with a colour picker built into the app rather than the operating system dialog.

exportPng.title: Export as an image
exportPng.body: The whole document as one tall PNG, ready to paste into a chat or a slide. The page is grown to the document height first, so nothing below the fold is quietly missing.

exportJson.title: Export as JSON
exportJson.body: Metadata, front matter, the outline, word counts, the Markdown and the parsed document tree — the same tree the editor itself works from, so a script sees exactly what MarkCraft sees.

share.title: Share and Export are on the title bar
share.body: Both were reachable only from the command palette, which is not where anyone looks for them.

previewLatency.title: The preview keeps pace with typing
previewLatency.body: It used to wait for a pause before updating, so a whole sentence could go by before the right-hand side moved. There is now a ceiling on how stale it can get, however fast you type.

recentOpensFolder.title: Recent and pinned files open their folder
recentOpensFolder.body: Choosing a remembered document now opens the folder it lives in, so the explorer shows its neighbours instead of something unrelated.

lastFolder.title: The folder you had open reopens
lastFolder.body: The record of the last workspace was being written to the wrong slot, which both lost the folder and overwrote that workspace’s saved tabs with an empty session. Both are fixed, so a restart puts you back where you were.

listContinuation.title: Enter continues a list
listContinuation.body: Two keymaps both bound Enter and the plain one always won, so pressing Enter in a list simply ended it instead of starting the next item.

toolbarCaret.title: The cursor lands after a toolbar marker
toolbarCaret.body: Starting a heading or a list on an empty line left the caret to the left of the marker it had just inserted, so the next thing you typed fell outside it.

modalLayering.title: Dropdowns inside Settings are visible
modalLayering.body: Menus, popovers and tooltips now paint above the surface they belong to. A select list opening behind the settings window was the visible symptom.

languageTemplate.title: “Export template…” works
languageTemplate.body: It asked for a file named after nothing the language loader accepts and was refused outright. The starter file is now named after the language code it contains.

present.title: Present straight from the document
present.body: F5 turns the open document into a deck. A line containing only --- is a slide break, so a document written for reading already presents sensibly. Arrow keys, Page Up/Down, Home and End move; Escape leaves. Slides render through the same pipeline as the preview, so a table or a diagram looks the same in both.

slashBlocks.title: Type / to insert a block
slashBlocks.body: A slash at the start of a line or after a space opens a menu of fourteen blocks — headings, lists, task lists, quotes, code, callouts, tables, links, images, emoji and dividers. Keep typing to narrow it; Enter or Tab inserts. It stays out of the way inside file paths, URLs and words like and/or. Both the English name and your own language match, so /heading and /başlıq both work.

devTools.title: Developer tools, offline
devTools.body: JSON formatting, JSON↔YAML, Base64, URL escaping, JWT decoding, timestamp conversion, a regular-expression tester and UUIDs — under Ctrl+Alt+T. All of it runs locally, which is the point: the text you paste in is usually a token, a config file or a customer’s payload, and pasting those into a web page is a habit worth breaking.

links.title: See how your documents connect
links.body: Ctrl+Alt+L scans the folder and draws the links between your documents, with the backlinks for whatever you are reading listed underneath and every broken link reported with its file and line. [[Wiki links]] resolve by file name from any folder; an ambiguous name is reported rather than guessed at.

website.title: Read your document at phone width
website.body: Ctrl+Alt+W shows the document as a page at 390, 768 and 1280 pixels — a real frame at that width, not a scaled picture, so the text wraps and the tables overflow exactly as they will for a reader.

imageEditor.title: Crop and compress before inserting
imageEditor.body: Picking a local image now offers a crop, a quality setting and a maximum width, with the resulting size shown while you decide. Compression re-encodes as WebP, which keeps transparency — a screenshot with a rounded corner survives it.

exportWordProcessor.title: Export to Word and rich text
exportWordProcessor.body: Two new formats: .docx for Word, Pages or Google Docs, and .rtf for anything else that reads formatted text. Headings, lists, task boxes, quotes and code all carry over, and both are generated from the same reading of your document so they cannot disagree.

callouts.title: Callouts
callouts.body: A blockquote beginning > [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION] renders as a coloured callout, in the editor and in every export.

emoji.title: An emoji picker
emoji.body: Ctrl+Alt+M, the toolbar, or /emoji. Search by name, with the ones you use most kept at the top.

headingIds.title: Headings get their own links
headingIds.body: Every heading is given an anchor using GitHub’s rules, so [](#a-section) works and a link into a document lands where it should. Non-Latin headings are handled properly.

codeCopy.title: Copy a code block in one click
codeCopy.body: Code blocks now show their language and a copy button, which copies the raw text rather than what the highlighter drew.

lintAndAudit.title: Find what is wrong before anyone else does
lintAndAudit.body: The statistics panel now reports broken internal links, duplicate heading anchors and nine Markdown problems that actually render wrong — a heading with no space after the hash, an unclosed code fence, an image with no alt text.

toolbarCustom.title: Choose what is on the toolbar
toolbarCustom.body: Settings now lets you pick which tools appear and in what order.

dropAnything.title: Drop anything onto the editor
dropAnything.body: Images are inserted, Markdown and text files are opened, and anything else is linked relatively.

startupSize.title: Faster to first paint
startupSize.body: The Markdown pipeline’s own dependencies were being loaded at startup along with the shell. Moving them to where they are actually needed took 330 kB out of the first paint.

functionKeys.title: Function keys work while you type
functionKeys.body: A shortcut with no modifier was handed to whatever text field had focus, which made F5 unreachable from the editor — the only place anyone presses it. Function keys cannot type a character, so they now reach the command they are bound to. Presentation mode also takes focus properly, so keys pressed while presenting no longer end up in the document.

book.title: A folder can be a book
book.body: Add a SUMMARY.md listing your chapters as a nested list of links and Ctrl+Alt+K reads the folder as one work — chapters in order, missing ones reported, and "Open as one document" combines them with each chapter’s headings shifted to its depth. It is the format mdBook and GitBook already use, so a book written here opens elsewhere.

study.title: Revise from the notes you already wrote
study.body: Write "Term :: meaning" on a line, or a question, a line containing only ?, and the answer — and that note is now revisable. The review session shows one card at a time and schedules the next sighting; a card keeps its history through any amount of rewriting around it, because it is identified by its own text.

canvas.title: Canvas
canvas.body: An infinite surface of cards and the lines between them, saved as JSON Canvas — the open format Obsidian writes, so a canvas made here opens there and the other way round. Cards render Markdown, and pan and zoom stay smooth with a hundred of them.

httpTester.title: Send an HTTP request
httpTester.body: For the API a technical document is about. Method, address, headers, body; status, timing and a pretty-printed response. Only http:// and https:// are accepted — checked again at every redirect — no cookies or credentials travel, and it fires only when you press the button.

runCode.title: Run a code block
runCode.body: A Run button on any fenced block in a language installed on this machine — JavaScript, Python, Ruby, PHP, Go, shell, PowerShell. The output appears under the block it came from. There is no sandbox and MarkCraft does not claim one: the code runs with your own permissions, exactly as it would if you had saved it and run it yourself, and it never runs on its own.

lock.title: Lock a document
lock.body: Turns editing off for the document you are reading — a guard against the accidental keystroke in something finished, signed off, or someone else’s. Checked at the save as well as in the editor, so autosave and "save all" respect it too.

streak.title: A writing streak
streak.body: The statistics panel now counts the days you wrote, with four weeks of squares. A streak that ended yesterday still counts today: someone who has not started this morning has not broken anything. The record holds a date and a number, never a filename.

pasteMarkdown.title: Paste web pages as Markdown
pasteMarkdown.body: Converts the clipboard’s formatted text through the same pipeline the preview uses, so headings, lists, tables and code survive — and a page’s navigation, banner and footer do not. A separate command rather than a hijack of Ctrl+V, which would do two different things depending on what you copied.

codeLanguage.title: Set a code block’s language
codeLanguage.body: From the command palette, while the caret is anywhere in the block — including one you have not closed yet, which is when you most want it. The list comes from the highlighter’s own table, so nothing is offered that cannot be coloured.

cleanUp.title: Clean up formatting
cleanUp.body: Repairs the four problems that have one correct answer: a heading jammed against its hashes, tabs, stray trailing spaces, an unclosed fence. The other five are left alone — inventing alt text or picking a language would edit meaning rather than form.

aiReview.title: Ask the AI to review, not rewrite
aiReview.body: A fifth AI action that reports findings instead of returning a document: structure that does not match the content, missing sections, claims left unexplained, headings that do not say what follows. Spelling and grammar are left to the checker that already does them.

quietLog.title: A quieter log
quietLog.body: Opening the canvas or the book panel in a folder that has neither no longer writes an error for something entirely routine. A log full of routine errors is a log nobody reads.
